routing.finding: Visibility, alerts, replenishment, and channel planning are independently covered.

interface_schema.finding: Planner, store, and category personas are explicit and identifiers are validated.

behavior.finding: Action commands were narrowed to review candidates and allocation is labeled a scenario.

safety.finding: All outputs are read-only; no stock is reserved, moved, replenished, allocated, promised, or purchased.

collateral_alignment.finding: The demo video shows a 51-location retailer whose Alpine Pro Winter Jacket is sold out in Portland while Seattle stores hold 247 excess units (Stores 1,847 / Warehouses 940 / In-transit 285 / E-comm 128), a two-phase Seattle -> Portland plan (120 units, $520, $18,400, 35:1), system-wide health (72/100, 43 days, $2.8M overstock, 147 stockouts/month, 8 more imbalances worth $84,200), warehouse automation (RFID $85K, auto-replenishment $45K, predictive allocation $32K, $340K/year) and a 3-year proposal ($162K, $1,020,000, $858,000); the agent had four Chicago stores, a stock review with zero alerts, days of supply divided by network-wide sales, and none of these operations.
collateral_alignment.fix: Re-seeded the network as the video's Pacific Northwest retailer with the hero SKU-2001, per-store daily sales (so Portland shows OUT_OF_STOCK/CRITICAL and Seattle OVERSTOCK with the nearest available store), and added NETWORK_ROLLUP, NEAREST_SOURCE, TRANSFER_PHASES, NETWORK_HEALTH, IMBALANCES, AUTOMATION_OPTIONS and INVENTORY_ACCURACY with computed totals plus the operations transfer_plan, network_health, automation_recommendations and investment_proposal (cases IV-05 to IV-08). Approvals return a release-ready packet; no stock moves and nothing is sent. ROI is computed as 530% (the video rounds to 531%) and Seattle's remaining 127 units are 31 days of supply at 4/day (the video says 8 weeks).
